cohort: 355 women with one prior cesarean delivery and no previous vaginal births, delivering either vaginally or by cesarean section
finding: Neonates born by cesarean delivery were more likely to have higher birth weight, weight at discharge, macrosomia, lose >10% of their body mass, be mixed-fed, and have longer hospitalizations, while children born vaginally were more likely to be exclusively breastfed.
mod_finding: Women undergoing VBAC were more likely to deliver preterm and post-term, present with PROM, have greater PROM latency period, and experience intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy, postpartum anemia, and peripartum blood loss >1 L.
